Are you familiar with the Newport News Circuit Court? Whether you’re a resident of Virginia or simply curious about the state’s judicial system, it’s important to understand the role and responsibilities of this court. Understanding Virginia’s Court System

Before delving into the specifics of the Newport News Circuit Court, it’s helpful to have a basic understanding of Virginia’s court system as a whole. Virginia’s judicial branch is divided into several different types of courts, including:

  • Circuit Courts
  • General District Courts
  • Juvenile and Domestic Relations District Courts
  • Virginia Court of Appeals
  • Supreme Court of Virginia

Each type of court has a distinct jurisdiction and handles different types of cases. The Newport News Circuit Court is one of Virginia’s circuit courts, which means it has a broad jurisdiction and hears a variety of different types of cases.

The History of the Newport News Circuit Court

The Newport News Circuit Court has a long and storied history that stretches back to the earliest days of the Commonwealth of Virginia. The court was originally established in 1896 as part of the city’s efforts to create a more centralized and efficient judicial system. Over the years, the court has grown and evolved to meet the changing needs of the community it serves.

The Structure of the Newport News Circuit Court

The Newport News Circuit Court is part of Virginia’s 7th Judicial Circuit, which also includes the circuit courts of Hampton, Williamsburg, and James City County. The court is presided over by one judge, who is elected by the Virginia General Assembly to an eight-year term.

The court is supported by a number of other staff members, including clerks, bailiffs, and other administrative personnel. These individuals work together to ensure that the court runs smoothly and efficiently.

The Functions of the Newport News Circuit Court

The Newport News Circuit Court has a broad jurisdiction and hears a variety of different types of cases, including:

  • Civil cases with claims greater than $25,000
  • Felony criminal cases
  • Juvenile criminal cases transferred from the Juvenile and Domestic Relations District Court
  • Appeals from the General District Court and Juvenile and Domestic Relations District Court
  • Various other types of cases as authorized by law

The court also has a number of other important functions, including:

  • Administering oaths and affirmations
  • Issuing marriage licenses
  • Registering deeds and other legal documents
  • Collecting fines and fees
